question.worked_solution:
First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{5}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{8{x}^{6}+5}{2{x}^{5}-7x} & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(\frac{8{x}^{6}}{{x}^{5}}+\frac{5}{{x}^{5}})}{(\frac{2{x}^{5}}{{x}^{5}}-\frac{7x}{{x}^{5}})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,\frac{(8x+\frac{5}{{x}^{5}})}{(2-\frac{7}{{x}^{4}})} \\  & =\frac{8x+0}{2-0} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\,\,4x \\  & =\infty .\end{aligned}
$$
